text.p: Argentina's consumer prices rose 0.5 percent in October, up from increases of 0.3 percent in October 1995 and 0.2 percent in September, the Economy Ministry said Monday.
Wholesale prices also rose 0.5 percent, compared with increases of 0.2 percent in October 1995 and 1.2 percent in September.
The consumer inflation rate was substantially lower than the range of 0.8 to 1.3 percent forecast by local analysts.
In the 12 months to October, consumer inflation was 0.4 percent, up from 0.2 percent in the 12 months to September.
Over the same period, wholesale prices rose 3.2 percent, compared with 2.7 percent in the 12 months to September 1995.
Analysts were predicting higher comsumer inflation mostly due to a steep rise in fuel prices, which pushed transport and communications rates up by eight percent in October.
But food and beverage prices dropped 0.6 percent, helping keep the overall rate at 0.5 percent.
Prices of goods and services and of household goods also fell, both by 0.1 percent, while health prices remained unchanged.

The fuel price hike, due to a fuel tax increase and a rise in crude oil prices, also was an important factor behind the 0.5 percent increase in October's wholesale prices, the ministry said in its monthly inflation report.
Wholesale prices of oil byproducts shot up 24.9 percent and of electricity 1.8 percent. But prices of other commodities fell by 3.7 percent and of imports by 0.5 percent.
